title: Citizens of Tournai bury victims of the plague
creator: Pierart dou Tielt (illuminator), in the Annals of Gilles Li Muisis
why_public_domain: Medieval manuscript illumination; creator died centuries ago, so copyright has long expired. OpenStax World History reuses it credited as Public Domain via Wikimedia Commons.
original_holder: Royal Library of Belgium (KBR), Brussels, MS 13076-77
caption: Townspeople of Tournai carry coffins and dig graves as the Black Death reaches Flanders in 1349. The abbot Gilles Li Muisis, who lived through the outbreak, had this scene painted into his chronicle.

title: The Dance of Death (Imago mortis)
creator: Michael Wolgemut (workshop), in Hartmann Schedel's Nuremberg Chronicle
why_public_domain: Fifteenth-century woodcut; copyright expired centuries ago. Credited Public Domain by OpenStax World History via Wikimedia Commons.
original_holder: Nuremberg Chronicle (printed book, many surviving copies)
caption: Skeletons dance on an open grave in this woodcut from the Nuremberg Chronicle. Nearly 150 years after the Black Death, Europeans still pictured death as a dancer who leads everyone away.

title: The Ploughman (The Husbandman), from The Dance of Death
creator: Hans Holbein the Younger (design); wood-engraved copy published by William Pickering
why_public_domain: Holbein died in 1543 and the 1833 London reproduction is far older than any copyright term; the scan is from Project Gutenberg eBook #38724 (Francis Douce, The Dance of Death), mirrored by GITenberg.
original_holder: Project Gutenberg / GITenberg (from Douce, The Dance of Death, London: William Pickering, 1833)
caption: Death runs beside a farmer's plough horses as the sun sets. Holbein drew the Dance of Death series in the 1520s, and by then death taking every rank of person was an old theme in European art.

title: Portrait of Sultan Mehmed II
creator: Gentile Bellini
why_public_domain: Painting by an artist who died in 1507; copyright long expired. Credited Public Domain by OpenStax World History via Wikimedia Commons.
caption: Mehmed II, who took Constantinople in 1453 at the age of 21, painted by the Venetian artist Gentile Bellini in 1480. The sultan had invited Bellini to his court in Istanbul.

title: View of Istanbul with the Fatih Mosque (detail of the Constantinople Prospect)
creator: Melchior Lorck
why_public_domain: Drawing by an artist who died after 1583; copyright long expired. Credited Public Domain by OpenStax World History via Wikimedia Commons.
caption: The Fatih Mosque, which Mehmed II built on the site of the Byzantine Church of the Holy Apostles, stands above the rooftops of Istanbul in Melchior Lorck's 1559 panorama. A Danish artist drew the city a century after the conquest.

title: Hagia Sophia, exterior view
creator: Unknown engraver (published 1857)
why_public_domain: Published in 1857, well before 1929. Credited Public Domain by OpenStax World History via Wikimedia Commons.
original_holder: Wikimedia Commons (via OpenStax World History, Volume 1)
caption: Hagia Sophia in 1857, with the minarets the Ottomans added after Mehmed II turned the great Byzantine church into a mosque in 1453. Its last Christian service was held on the night before the city fell.

title: Departure of John III Sobieski and Marysieńka Sobieska from Wilanów
creator: Józef Brandt
why_public_domain: Brandt died in 1915, more than 70 years ago, and the painting was made before 1929. Standard Ebooks cleared it for the cover of Sienkiewicz's The Deluge; this is their cropped cover image.
original_holder: Standard Ebooks (cover of The Deluge); painting's current holder not stated in the source
caption: King John III Sobieski and Queen Marysieńka leave Wilanów Palace by torchlight, as Józef Brandt imagined the scene two centuries later. In 1683 Sobieski led the cavalry charge that broke the Ottoman siege of Vienna.

title: The Lisbon earthquake, tsunami and fire of 1 November 1755
creator: Unknown engraver (hand-coloured copper engraving)
date: 1755 (as commonly attributed; the colouring may be later)
why_public_domain: Eighteenth-century print; copyright long expired. The provenance is weaker than for the other images: this copy is reposted on a blog (dox-lab.github.io), where it is credited only to a secondary website. It matches the engraving usually cited as the Kozák Collection print (NISEE, UC Berkeley).
original_holder: Commonly attributed to the Jan Kozák Collection, NISEE, University of California, Berkeley (not confirmed from this copy)
caption: Lisbon burns while a tsunami sweeps ships from the harbour onto crowds fleeing along the waterfront. Prints like this spread news of the 1755 disaster across Europe within weeks.

title: The Forum of Pompeii, looking toward Vesuvius
creator: Unknown photographer (Plate I in August Mau, Pompeii: Its Life and Art)
why_public_domain: Photograph published in 1899 in August Mau, 'Pompeii: Its Life and Art' (trans. Francis W. Kelsey, Macmillan, New York); published before 1929, so public domain in the US. Copy from the Project Gutenberg edition (ebook #42715) mirrored by GITenberg.
original_holder: Project Gutenberg / GITenberg (from the 1899 Macmillan edition)
caption: The excavated Forum of Pompeii, with Vesuvius rising behind it. The mountain that buried the town in 79 CE still overlooks its ruins.

title: Vesuvius as seen from Naples
creator: Unknown photographer (Fig. 2 in August Mau, Pompeii: Its Life and Art)
why_public_domain: Photograph published in 1899 in August Mau, 'Pompeii: Its Life and Art' (trans. Francis W. Kelsey, Macmillan, New York); published before 1929, so public domain in the US. Copy from the Project Gutenberg edition (ebook #42715) mirrored by GITenberg.
original_holder: Project Gutenberg / GITenberg (from the 1899 Macmillan edition)
caption: Vesuvius across the Bay of Naples, with a thin plume of steam at its summit. From this shore in 79 CE, Pliny the Elder set out across the bay toward the eruption.

title: Plaster cast of a man who died at Pompeii
creator: Unknown photographer (Fig. 7 in August Mau, Pompeii: Its Life and Art)
why_public_domain: Photograph published in 1899 in August Mau, 'Pompeii: Its Life and Art' (trans. Francis W. Kelsey, Macmillan, New York); published before 1929, so public domain in the US. Copy from the Project Gutenberg edition (ebook #42715) mirrored by GITenberg.
original_holder: Project Gutenberg / GITenberg (from the 1899 Macmillan edition)
caption: Excavators poured plaster into the hollow left in the hardened ash by a man's body, recovering the position in which he fell. Casts like this one are the closest we come to the faces of the people of Pompeii.

title: Joseph Stalin, July 1941
creator: Unknown Soviet photographer
why_public_domain: Anonymous Soviet photograph of 1941, credited by OpenStax World History to Nationaal Archief (Netherlands) via Wikimedia Commons, marked Public Domain. Under Russian law at the time, anonymous works expired 50 years after publication (1991), before the 1996 URAA restoration date, so it is also treated as public domain in the US. Weaker than the other entries: no named photographer, and it dates from 1941, not 1937.
original_holder: Nationaal Archief, The Hague (per the OpenStax credit)
caption: Joseph Stalin waves from a reviewing stand in 1941. Four years earlier, at the height of the Great Terror, his signature appeared on lists condemning tens of thousands to death.

title: Gandhi collecting salt at Dandi, Salt March
creator: Unknown photographer
why_public_domain: Anonymous 1930 photograph from British India, credited by OpenStax World History as 'Salt March' by Unknown/Wikimedia Commons, Public Domain. Indian photographs expired 60 years after publication (1990), before the 1996 URAA date, so it is also public domain in the US. Context image only: it shows the independence movement 17 years before Partition, not Partition itself.
caption: Gandhi stoops to gather salt on the shore at Dandi in 1930, defying the British salt tax. The independence movement he led ended British rule in 1947, but it could not hold the subcontinent together.

title: Buzz Aldrin and the US flag on the Moon (AS11-40-5875)
creator: Neil A. Armstrong, NASA
why_public_domain: Photograph taken by a NASA astronaut / NASA employee as part of official duties; works of the US federal government are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
caption: Buzz Aldrin stands beside the flag at Tranquility Base, with the lunar module Eagle at left. The bootprints in the foreground were the first human tracks on another world.

title: Bootprint in the lunar soil (AS11-40-5878)
creator: Edwin E. 'Buzz' Aldrin Jr., NASA
why_public_domain: Photograph taken by a NASA astronaut / NASA employee as part of official duties; works of the US federal government are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
caption: Aldrin photographed his own bootprint to study how the fine lunar dust held its shape. With no wind or rain, the print is likely still there.

title: Official portrait of the Apollo 11 crew
creator: NASA
why_public_domain: Photograph taken by a NASA astronaut / NASA employee as part of official duties; works of the US federal government are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
caption: Neil Armstrong, Michael Collins and Buzz Aldrin in their official crew portrait. Collins stayed in lunar orbit while the other two walked on the Moon.

title: Lunar highlands photographed from orbit by the Apollo 11 crew
creator: Apollo 11 crew, NASA
why_public_domain: Photograph taken by a NASA astronaut / NASA employee as part of official duties; works of the US federal government are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
caption: Cratered highlands seen from lunar orbit during Apollo 11. On the far side of each orbit Michael Collins was out of radio contact with Earth, alone in Columbia.

title: Ronald Reagan speaking at the Brandenburg Gate
creator: White House Photographic Office
why_public_domain: Official White House photograph taken by a federal employee; works of the US federal government are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105).
original_holder: Ronald Reagan Presidential Library, National Archives
caption: President Reagan speaks in front of the Berlin Wall and the Brandenburg Gate in June 1987, calling on Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev to 'tear down this wall.' Two and a half years later, Berliners began tearing it down themselves.

title: George H. W. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev dine at the Malta Summit
creator: White House photographer
why_public_domain: Official White House photograph taken by a federal employee; credited by OpenStax American Government to the National Archives and Records Administration. Works of the US federal government are public domain (17 U.S.C. 105). Cropped from panel (b) of a two-panel OpenStax figure.
original_holder: George H. W. Bush Presidential Library, National Archives
caption: Mikhail Gorbachev (left) and George H. W. Bush (right) at dinner during the Malta Summit, three weeks after the Wall opened. Their talks are often taken as the moment the Cold War began to end.
